name: fanotify_init
synopsis: int fanotify_init(unsigned int flags, unsigned int event_flags);
description: fanotify_init() initializes a new fanotify group and returns a file descriptor for the event queue associated with the group. This descriptor is used to monitor specified filesystem objects and receive events via fanotify_mark(2).

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Defines the notification class (e.g., FAN_CLASS_PRE_CONTENT, FAN_CLASS_CONTENT, FAN_CLASS_NOTIF) and behavior flags (e.g., FAN_CLOEXEC) for the fanotify group.

parameters.name: event_flags
parameters.description: Additional flags for event reporting, such as FAN_REPORT_FID or FAN_REPORT_PIDFD, which modify the types of events generated.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: An invalid value was passed in flags or event_flags.
The number of fanotify groups for this user exceeds the limit, or the per-process limit on open file descriptors has been reached.
The allocation of memory for the notification group failed.
This kernel does not implement fanotify_init().
The caller lacks a required capability.

bugs: Bugs present before Linux 3.18: O_CLOEXEC is ignored in event_flags. Bugs present before Linux 3.14: event_flags argument is not checked for invalid flags, allowing unintended internal flags.
versions: Available since Linux 2.6.37; prior to Linux 5.13, required CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability.
